Edit a terminal command in visual mode

by Connor Kuljis

In bash edit the current command line in your default editor, you can use the following key sequence:

Enter normal mode by pressing ESC, then press v

This requires set -o vi in your .bashrc.

Or

Press C-x C-e to open your current command line with your default editor.

Example

https://go.dev/doc/install

Remove any previous Go installation by deleting the /usr/local/go folder (if it exists), then extract the archive you just downloaded into /usr/local, creating a fresh Go tree in /usr/local/go:
$ rm -rf /usr/local/go && tar -C /usr/local -xzf go1.24.4.linux-amd64.tar.gz
(You may need to run each command separately with the necessary permissions, as root or through sudo.)

When I copied the command to my terminal, I realized that I had to edit the command line before executing it. Usually this would mean navigating my curor to the correct position using the arrow keys, and appending sudo to each command. Instead, I used the C-x C-e key sequence to open the command in my default editor, which allowed me to easily add sudo before each command without having to navigate through the command line.

sudo rm -rf /usr/local/go && \
sudo tar -C /usr/local -xzf ~/Downloads/go1.24.4.linux-amd64.tar.gz
